text:
Maya: Ran a focused smokebench for embed/rerank endpoints — reproducer and short summary below. TL;DR: p99 tail latency regressed ~30% after kernel routing change (commit abc123) on A100s when KV cache is cold and effective batch size >64. 

Simon: ugh. which harness did you run? synthetic or replay?

Maya: both. synthetic harness used `wrk`-style driver with gaussian interarrival, replay used the replay-harness that replays traffic from prod-sampled traces. numbers: synthetic p50~45ms p99~210ms, replay p50~50ms p99~280ms. baseline before abc123 was p99~210ms (replay) so repro is pretty consistent.

Lee: grabbed perf profiles on the failing config. main hotspot is kernel_selection fallback path + extra memcpy for KV evictions. flamegraph attached in gist: https://gists.example.com/lee/embed-rerank-flame. Looks like we call the generic matmul kernel for seq_len>512 instead of the fused fp16 kernel.

Frank: repro steps I used (quick):
```
# run replay harness with 5k concurrent users, clip to 2k QPS
./replay_harness --trace=sampled_traces.jl --qps=2000 --concurrency=5000 \n  --endpoint=/v1/embed-rerank --payload-scale=1.2 --vector-dim=768
```
Toggle KV cache warm/cold via the `--kv-warm` flag (true/false).

Ananya: also tried varying vector dims: 768 vs 1536. 1536 increases p99 by ~40-60ms across the board (expected) but the regression delta after abc123 is proportionally larger for 1536 (kernel routing misses are more expensive). Payload size (extra metadata per item) adds ~5-15ms depending on serialization path.

Maya: key observations I want to capture for the issue: list format
- Regression correlated with kernel routing change (abc123) that added heuristic: prefer kernel B for seq_len>=384 on A100.
- When KV cache is cold (many misses + hot reloads) we see repeated memcpy and fallback to slower kernel; effects compound with larger batches.
- Replay harness shows slightly worse tail than synthetic because of burstiness and real interarrival patterns.
- Smaller batches (<=32) mostly unaffected; >64 shows p99 spike.

Simon: can we set a targeted test matrix for next run? propose: 
- vector dims: [768, 1536]
- batch sizes: [1,16,32,64,128]
- kv state: [cold, warm]
- kernel routing: [pre-abc123, post-abc123] (we can force by env var)
That should be 2x5x2x2 = 40 runs. automated with the replay harness runner.

Lee: i'll add perf collection (perf, nvprof, and runtime flamegraphs) for each run. small ask: pin to single GPU to avoid cross-GPU scheduling noise.

Frank: FYI the replay harness has a `--inject-arrival-variance` flag. Use 0.3 to mimic prod burstiness — that makes tail reveal itself. Example runner: 
```
./run_matrix.sh --dims "768,1536" --batches "1,16,32,64,128" \n  --kv "cold,warm" --kernels "pre,post" --qps=2000 --arrival-var=0.3
```
I'll drop the script in the infra repo after i clean it up.

Ananya: small note re apples-to-apples: ensure that the model quant/precision is identical across runs (fp16 vs int8) and that cutover doesn't trigger a lazy compilation step (nvrtc) mid-run. precompile all kernels or run a 2-minute warmup.

Maya: opened GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/4521 with the initial numbers and steps. tagging @simon @lee @frank for follow-up.

ops-bot: deploy-notify: canary rollout of commit abc123 to dedicated-a100 pool started at 2025-11-12T14:02:10Z :information_source: 

Simon: i'll schedule the 40-run matrix on staging GPUs tonight and attach results CSV. If we confirm kernel bug, plan is to revert heuristic and instead add a microbenchmark-driven selector.

Lee: one more gotcha — KV cache eviction is implemented in the runtime thread which sometimes blocks the main serving thread for ~2-3ms spikes when large entries are evicted. We should audit evict path (stream memcpy off main thread).

Maya: perfect. next actions:
1) Simon runs matrix and uploads CSV to issue.
2) Lee collects perf traces for worst offenders.
3) Frank posts run script in infra.
4) Ananya verifies warmup/compilation controls.
5) I'll draft a short regression postmortem if we confirm the root cause.

Maya: thanks all :heart:
